symptom: The Draft 2020-12 Shadow Evidence schema used dollar end anchors for generatedAt, scope.from, scope.to and SHA-256 digests. Python jsonschema 4.26 uses re.search, where a terminal LF is admitted before dollar, whereas the runtime rejects noncanonical date/time strings and digest mismatches. Synthetic newline-only probes reproduced the cross-engine lexical gap; no private values or production records were used.
lesson: Regex dollar anchors are not a portable exact-end guard across JSON Schema implementations: Python re.search admits one trailing LF while ECMAScript RegExp does not. Schema-only validation can therefore accept noncanonical metadata even when the runtime rejects it. This is lexical validation only, not proof of timestamp authority or source trust.
guardrail: Use a portable negative-lookahead end assertion (?![\s\S]) for canonical Shadow Evidence generatedAt, scope.from/to and SHA-256 schema patterns. Add explicit terminal LF/CRLF, Unicode line terminator and valid-control regressions; retain runtime Gregorian roundtrip, digest equality and research/production separation. Avoid brittle tests that forbid legitimate [\s\S] interior classes.
